definition: Web intelligence is the area of scientific research and development that explores the roles and makes use of artificial intelligence and information technology for new products, services and frameworks that are empowered by the World Wide Web.
details: The term was coined in a paper written by Ning Zhong, Jiming Liu Yao and Y.Y. Ohsuga in the Computer Software and Applications Conference in 2000.

explainer.lead: Web intelligence is the research field studying how AI and information technology can be applied to the World Wide Web to produce new products, services and frameworks. It matters because it frames the web as both a data source and a platform for intelligent systems.

tiers.eli5: It is the study of how to make the web smart, so that websites and services can understand what you want instead of just showing you pages.
tiers.practitioner: Practitioners work at the intersection of web data, agents and user modelling, building services that adapt to users rather than serving static pages. The pitfall is scope creep: the field is broad, so projects need a concrete product or service target.
tiers.paperLevel: The term was coined in a 2000 paper by Ning Zhong, Jiming Liu Yao and Y.Y. Ohsuga at the Computer Software and Applications Conference, describing AI and IT applied to web-empowered products, services and frameworks. It names an area of research rather than a single formal method.

explainer.example: A recommendation service that learns from browsing behaviour to personalise what a user sees is an example of a web-empowered intelligent product in this field.
